automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.date_policy: Only sources visibly published or updated within the last 7 days qualified; missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, and boundary-only dates were excluded.

selection_basis: New or unchecked leaves first, then oldest last_checked_at, ties by stable relative path sort; excluded index, digest, broad maintenance, federation, schema, glossary, known-defects, open-decisions, maintenance-log, topic-index, and dated source-synthesis pages unless durable local practice leaves.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The MCP roadmap prioritizes agentic messaging primitives, server-initiated events, HTTP-native transport hardening, agent identity/delegation, clearer tool-call result shapes, progressive discovery, primitive annotations, and generated SDK/conformance work.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local MCP/tool leaves should treat protocol roadmap items as deployment-lifecycle signals: async tasks, progressive discovery, identity, cache semantics, and tool result shapes need conformance evidence before teams expand local tool access.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Speakeasy defines skills governance as live tracking of every agent skill, including file identity, owner, loading agents, sanctioned status, and which tools the skill directs agents to call; it warns that skill files can evade normal software asset registers.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local skill and rules-layer pages should treat SKILL.md-style files as governed operational assets, with owner, approval, tool-scope, and registry evidence rather than informal prompt snippets.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article argues that production agents need software-discipline controls around prompts and tools: versioning, review, testing, documentation, ownership, componentized responsibilities, regression gates, rollback paths, tool-call tracing, and explicit automation boundaries.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Several local practice leaves can reuse this as public evidence that prompts, durable instructions, tool calls, and autonomy boundaries should be managed like production software behavior.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Snowflake emphasized governed enterprise AI deployment with trusted data, shared business context, model flexibility, cost controls, Horizon Context, Snowflake CoCo/CoWork, and Cortex AI Gateway visibility and access management.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local implication is context-first analytics governance: semantic business meaning, access scope, cost telemetry, and model routing should be prerequisites before self-service data agents answer operational questions.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Firecrawl describes agent-oriented academic search requirements: stable paper identity, in-body supporting passages rather than abstracts only, structured metadata, citation graph traversal, freshness, and rate limits that survive multi-hop loops.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Deep research and RAG leaves should require identity, passage-level evidence, citation relationships, and loop-suitable rate limits when research agents need verifiable citations.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CodeRabbit argues that AI-generated pull requests increase review volume and make the PR carry more context: issue rationale, agent activity, tests, security findings, review debate, approval records, semantic change grouping, and human ownership of the result.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Delegated coding handoffs and structural review should preserve intent, evidence, risk triage, semantic grouping, and accountable approval instead of treating an agent diff as self-explanatory.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The paper reports a dataset of 248,641 AI-attributed GitHub PRs that received AI-attributed reviews, including 45,269 cross-product reviews and 208,145 same-product reviews; closed-loop AI-to-AI review is increasing but remains a minority of identified agent activity.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: AI-generated code review practice should keep author-agent and reviewer-agent identity, review configuration, latency, and output differences visible because review evidence can vary by product pairing.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Stack Overflow frames agentic development around the cost tradeoff between underspecified prompts and overlarge specs, recommending enough structure, examples, executable checks, spec validation, typed contracts, validators, and expiration of stale design prose.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Workflow and handoff leaves should preserve the right level of specification for the work type and treat multi-agent boundaries as explicit contracts with testable validation.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Augment describes AI code review as a CI/CD workflow triggered by pull-request events, extracting diffs, invoking review prompts, posting PR comments, and using permissions and allowed tools to scope the review action.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Event-triggered and structural-review leaves should treat PR review bots as controlled workflow runs with trigger payloads, repository permissions, allowed tools, comments, and merge-gate evidence.

qualifying_updates.visible_date: Week of August 25, 2026; items dated August 20-23, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The weekly agent news page records recent items about versioned coding-agent CLI releases, A2A joining AAIF under neutral governance, Bedrock AgentCore Web Search GA, Gemini Enterprise platform consolidation, and Snowflake CoCo Automations public preview with inspectable Cortex threads.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Treat as routed evidence: broad product/protocol news is upstream-owned, while the local implication is to pin agent CLI versions, test release channels, preserve inspectable long-running task receipts, and compare retrieval/governance controls before adopting agent platforms.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Mastra compares agent access, governance, and integration platforms around identity, workflow, and integration architecture rather than treating agent access as a simple connector catalog.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local governance implication is to evaluate agent-access platforms by identity, authorization, integration scope, and workflow fit, while routing vendor-by-vendor product background upstream.
